title: Apple partners with OpenEvidence to launch health AI research app, plans to recruit 200,000 users

content_html:
Apple has announced a partnership with OpenEvidence, a healthcare AI company, to launch an AI research app for the health sector, aimed at studying how artificial intelligence can provide users with health information and medical guidance based on clinical evidence. The app is now available for download to users in the United States, and Apple plans to recruit approximately 200,000 participants for a study lasting more than 12 months.

In terms of eligibility, users must be at least 21 years old, use an iPhone 15 or later, run iOS 26 or later, and have Apple Intelligence enabled. The app lets users ask health questions much like they would with ChatGPT or Claude, and answers will be based on clinical and scientific literature such as the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, and Nature, helping users understand everyday medical issues. Users can also rate answers, submit feedback, and take part in monthly surveys.

In addition, users can choose to share resting heart rate, activity, sleep data, and lab results from HealthKit to receive more targeted recommendations. The app also supports preparation for medical visits and recommendations for healthcare providers. Apple said user data will be anonymized before being sent to third-party cloud services, will not be used to train AI models, and OpenEvidence will delete query and response data after 24 hours.

This time, Apple has not directly launched a medical AI assistant for the general public. Instead, it is using long-term research to assess the practical value of AI in health scenarios and to accumulate clinical and user data for future related products and services.
